OpenOnco is a free, open-source clinical: OpenOnco is a free, open-source clinical decision support resource for oncology tumor boards. A deterministic rule engine over a versioned, source-cited knowledge base drafts two alternative treatment plans (standard and aggressive) for the treating oncologist to verify. It is informational support requiring qualified clinician review; the Charter does not establish regulatory classification.
No large language model picks the regime: No large language model picks the regimen or dose in OpenOnco. All clinical logic is a deterministic rule engine over a versioned, source-cited knowledge base, and every recommendation carries a source citation, so it requires clinical verification of inputs, sources and outputs.

## Disclaimer

OpenOnco is an informational resource to support tumor-board discussion. It is
for review with a qualified oncologist. Every
recommendation must be verified by the treating physician with the full clinical
picture and discussed by a multidisciplinary team (CHARTER §11 + §15).

OpenOnco applies checked-in YAML rules to structured oncology profiles and
produces source-cited drafts for clinician review. Try a synthetic example
without signup, inspect its sources in Onco Wiki, or run the Python engine.
Deterministic output can still be wrong: clinical content is provisional,
and a qualified oncologist must verify every recommendation.

The Plan Builder runs the Python engine through Pyodide in the browser.
The separate Tumor Board service can send submitted information to its
server; review that page's data notice before entering information.

own licenses. This is an informational resource for qualified clinician review.

rule/source mismatches on synthetic profiles. Do not post patient data.
